findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permission denied, empty path)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path crashes the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use ? to propagate; never unwrap fallible I/O

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input (e.g. "abc") or empty lines
findings.failure_mode: a single malformed line in the data file aborts the entire session load instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use ? on parse::<u32>() and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>; or map_err with a domain-specific error type

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values > 65535; uses `as` instead of u16::try_from
findings.failure_mode: a u32 value of 70000 becomes 4464 in u16 with zero warning, corrupting session data silently
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_value)? which returns an error for out-of-range values instead of silent truncation

findings.problem: parts[0] indexes the vec without bounds check; split on ',' produces at most 1 element if no comma exists
findings.failure_mode: a line with no comma panics with index-out-of-bounds on parts[0] or parts[1]
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') which returns (before, after) or None, handling missing commas gracefully with ?

findings.problem: parts[1] indexes the vec without bounds check; a line with only one comma-separated field has no parts[1]
findings.failure_mode: a line like "session_name," or a line with a single field panics on parts[1] access
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the None case; extract field 1 from the (before, after) tuple with a default or error

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> just to index elements; split_once is the prescribed pattern
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation and string cloning for every line; violates zero-cost abstraction discipline
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (&str, &str) without allocation, then trim and parse each piece independently

findings.problem: println! is hidden I/O inside a function whose signature is load_sessions(path: &str) -> Vec<Record>, mixing side effects into data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: the function signature promises a pure data transformation but silently writes to stdout, making it untestable and breaking functional core purity; logging in the shell leaks into the data layer
findings.fix: Remove the println! from load_sessions; if logging is needed, return the records and let the shell layer decide whether to log

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all fallible operations inside (read, parse, convert) are hidden behind unwrap
findings.failure_mode: every possible failure mode is a panic; the caller has no way to distinguish file-not-found from parse-error from overflow
findings.fix: Change signature to fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> where LoadError is a domain error enum covering I/O and parse variants

findings.problem: collect() into Vec<String> for every line allocates heap memory that is unnecessary when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unbounded memory allocation per line; for large files this is wasteful and unpredictable
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get borrowed &str pairs, trim and parse directly without collecting into Vec<String>
